about: READ-ONLY: the cluster's orphan set — every live object in the managed namespaces that no manifest under infra/cluster/manifests declares — as `infra/cluster/undeclared-objects.sh --list` computes it, the ONE definition the orphan lint and delete-orphan-object share, followed by ONE verdict line the judging rule reads: `verdict: clean` at zero undeclared objects, `verdict: <n> undeclared object(s)` otherwise, `verdict: unanswered (...)` when the derivation refused (exit 4, 'cannot answer' with the reason named, never a smaller set) — the wrapper infra/cluster/conformance-report.sh draws it, because in --list the derivation's stdout IS the orphan set and cannot carry a verdict (backlog 970c0c94). Filed by the cluster-conformance sweep for itself the moment its Inspect step becomes ready (rule measure-cluster-conformance-sweep-on-inspect-ready, backlog 8e8311f5): on 2026-09-12 the inspector had to gather this by hand from a credential that could not read half the pairs, and the sweep before it sat uninspected; since 2026-09-18 a clean verdict completes that Inspect step by rule (judge-cluster-conformance-sweep-on-report-answered). Nothing mutated; the same kubectl and kubeconfig resolution as the delete verb, without the delete. Its own timeout: the derivation parses every manifest with kubectl, which exceeds the runner's 30s default.
